text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience significant pain in the wound or surrounding area, and does the skin around the wound appear discolored or hardened? Also, have you noticed any weeping or drainage from the wound?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is there brownish discoloration or hardening of the skin around the wound, and does the wound bed appear moist with granulation tissue? I would also like to request a vascular assessment to check for venous insufficiency. REQUEST TEST: Venous_Duplex_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Inspection reveals discolored skin around the wound with evidence of chronic changes such as pigmentation. Doppler Ultrasound of the lower limb demonstrates evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in the superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms venous insufficiency, which aligns with your history of DVT and chronic swelling. Given the discolored skin and location of the wound, this is consistent with venous stasis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer
